This case isn't new. A three-judge panel found that Alabama's maps violated the VRA in 2022, and the Supreme Court agreed in 2023. Alabama used the court-mandated nonpartisan map in 2024, then turned right around to try and put their gerrymandered, suppressive map back in place for 2026.
When voters are silenced and votes are suppressed anywhere our democracy is harmed everywhere. Pitch in $25 or more right now to spread the word about this case and fight for fair maps nationwide >> [https://secure.everyaction.com/Z31SNww9Q0CZWIdx46cuSQ2?am=25.00&contactdata=r6NwY4gc12GQmzWj4fZPZRGlOlV1qmvpcE/z9yLRswloBy8Njz/PkScVJgssNp74+K/8cla0wDtMIs9vgVLsctx34ZNcfMVahPIO13bFS24=]
AP: Alabama’s congressional map at stake in federal Voting Rights Act trial [https://secure.everyaction.com/Z31SNww9Q0CZWIdx46cuSQ2?am=20.00&contactdata=r6NwY4gc12GQmzWj4fZPZRGlOlV1qmvpcE/z9yLRswloBy8Njz/PkScVJgssNp74+K/8cla0wDtMIs9vgVLsctx34ZNcfMVahPIO13bFS24=]
Folks,
Alabama’s congressional map is at stake in a federal trial that wil decide if the state will keep the new court-created district that led to the election of a second Black representative. From the AP:
" A three-judge panel will decide whether congressional lines drawn by state lawmakers diluted the voting power of Black residents. The same panel already ruled against Alabama in pre-trial decisions that reshaped the 2nd Congressional District before Rep. Shomari Figures won election in November, giving Alabama two Black representatives in its delegation for the first time in history. "
The state of Alabama is seeking to reinstate the maps created by the suppressive state legislature. This case began in 2021 when Black voters and civil rights groups filed lawsuits over Alabama’s state-drawn congressional map they said disenfranchised Black voters.
Team, we have to make sure voters everywhere know about this case to protect fair maps in court. Please pitch in $25 or whatever you can to help us make every vote count, either at the ballot box or in court >> [https://secure.everyaction.com/Z31SNww9Q0CZWIdx46cuSQ2?am=25.00&contactdata=r6NwY4gc12GQmzWj4fZPZRGlOlV1qmvpcE/z9yLRswloBy8Njz/PkScVJgssNp74+K/8cla0wDtMIs9vgVLsctx34ZNcfMVahPIO13bFS24=]

Defenders of voting rights believe they can show a level of continuing, intentional discrimination that should once again make Alabama subject to the preclearance requirement of the 1965 Voting Rights Act.
Deuel Ross, an attorney with the NAACP Legal Defense Fund who represents the plaintiffs seeking to protect the current map, said " This is sort of exactly the thing that Alabama and other states did before the Voting Rights Act — a court would find that there was some sort of discrimination in the way in which they were drawing maps or registering voters and the state would respond by essentially doing the same thing over again, but dressing it up in a slightly different outfit ".
Attacks like this on what remains of the Voting Rights Act are going to get worse over the next few years. As voter suppression laws become increasingly targeted and gerrymandering more oppressive , our work to defend the right to vote must become smarter, stronger, and more accessible to everyone.
We can't do this alone. body:
When we think about the people who have done the most to support VoteVets over the years, it’s not the people who write the biggest checks who come to mind.
#
Peter -
When we think about the people who have done the most to support VoteVets over the years, it’s not the people who write the biggest checks who come to mind.
It’s the people who were there when everything was on the line
Like you, Peter.

Your support, voice, and participation have helped us run some of the most powerful and impactful ads out there. Your support helps us win races and pass legislation that improves lives.
Thanks to you we’ve won races that wouldn’t even be competitive.
It’s helped us fight for things that matter most to Veterans. We’ve killed repeated efforts to privatize the VA, to cut or shortchange care. It passed the PACT Act and expanded care to millions. It got hundreds of Veterans and National Security professionals elected last year, and they are the ones holding the line against Trump now.

But here’s an interesting fact: out of almost 2 million people who have taken action with VoteVets, only 1% have made a donation online to support our work.
Today, we’re asking you to join that select group.

Our average donation is $25. Some give more, many give less. But with the VA under attack like never before in its history, with Veterans being fired across the government, and with our commitment to our allies in question, all that matters is that you are chipping in to an organization that is leading the fight against Donald Trump every single day.
We’ll put it right to work fighting and defeating these liars and hypocrites in the most important moment in modern American political history — the one we’re in right now.

name: Andrew Yang
subject: A War of Our Own
body:
This self-inflicted trade war is one of the dumbest things I’ve ever seen. | |
---
| | |
---
| [ ](https://yangspeaks.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7448319cdb745ea2fd1b1b8a8&id=7b7c4ac354&e=0f227c2ae3)
---
|
---
| [ ](https://yangspeaks.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7448319cdb745ea2fd1b1b8a8&id=e7575c89ce&e=0f227c2ae3)
---
| “I didn’t think Trump would actually implement tariffs; I thought it was a negotiating tactic.”

I’ve seen this sentiment aired a hundred times both publicly and privately. It has been incredibly frustrating watching Trump launch a trade war. His tariffs are going to be vastly destructive and will raise prices for consumers and manufacturers alike. Agricultural states and the Midwest are going to be hit particularly hard, but every American will feel the pinch when they head to the store. The result has already started to weigh on global stock markets as less trade and more uncertainty make it harder to invest in growth. Trump’s vacillating on what the tariffs cover doesn’t help; who could plan investments not knowing if it’s going to change week to week?

Also, Wednesday was the announcement that US employers announced plans to cut 172,000 jobs in February, the highest number since July 2020 and the 12th highest in 32 years. This included 62,000 federal employees, a number which will obviously increase. Trump’s plans to cut 80,000 workers from the VA alone recently leaked.

One thing that has been supporting the stock market for months is “the AI trade.” Of course, AI itself is a job suppressor; I know a dozen executives who have either cut jobs or didn’t hire workers directly because of AI.

One pattern that recurs is that employers tend not to be in the practice of shedding workers until a recession hits. Then, they look around and become ruthless on headcount, in part because the economic environment gives them cover to do so. Imagine companies in job-cutting mode fueled by AI? That’s fast approaching.

Indeed, February’s layoff numbers as well as a very weak Fed survey indicate that we may be teetering on the edge of a recession right now. The twin spectre of a trade war and widespread federal layoffs that will leave tens of thousands of households in professional and financial limbo are weakening confidence. The NIH and USAID cuts have already had that kind of impact on thousands of researchers and non-profit workers.

Trump seems more than ready to inflict economic pain on the country he leads. It’s bizarre.

This self-inflicted trade war is one of the dumbest things I’ve ever seen. Do I think Trump is leading us into a recession through his tariffs, posturing and erratic leadership? Yes. Yes I do. And I think this one will feel different compared to any of the recent ones we have experienced.

This week on the [podcast](https://yangspeaks.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7448319cdb745ea2fd1b1b8a8&id=5a5c8034e6&e=0f227c2ae3) I sit down with our friend John Avlon to talk policy. Also, a state [senator](https://yangspeaks.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7448319cdb745ea2fd1b1b8a8&id=f59b89a7a5&e=0f227c2ae3) in Utah joined Forward this week, our 47th elected official to affiliate! An [article](https://yangspeaks.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7448319cdb745ea2fd1b1b8a8&id=14ae16a472&e=0f227c2ae3) in the Bulwark this week pointed out that a new party could compete in areas that are currently uncompetitive; it’s exactly what the country needs. New people are joining Forward all the time – [check](https://yangspeaks.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7448319cdb745ea2fd1b1b8a8&id=cba11f23e3&e=0f227c2ae3) out what we are doing in your state.
---

Andrew Yang**

* **TOP NEWS**

"**ICE arrests over 640 in Houston, says most accused of crimes** ," Houston Chronicle's **Matt deGrood** -- "More than 640 people allegedly in the country without permission -- 550 of which were accused of crimes -- [were arrested in the Houston area](https://substack.com/redirect/dd8d3859-642d-4fbd-a0aa-7ba54594d4be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during an operation that began in late February, federal officials said Monday.

The arrests came as part of a targeted operation between Feb. 23 and March 2 meant to help public safety and national and border security, according to a spokesperson for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The dates coincide with a [deportation in Colony Ridge](https://substack.com/redirect/48f72ecd-e14f-426e-a1f9-093f4de4f398?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that began with an [announcement](https://substack.com/redirect/9e78c5b2-0c81-48dc-af7a-4f7ab86a04b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Texas Gov. **Greg Abbott**.

"These collective efforts have made our local communities significantly safer and strengthened our national security and border security," said **Chad Plantz** , special agent in charge for Homeland Security Investigations in Houston, in a prepared statement.

Federal officials have been mostly mum about the specifics of their actions across the Houston region in recent weeks. In Monday's announcement, they said federal investigators had executed 71 warrants and arrested more than 543 people accused of crimes and seven gang members as part of the operation. They did not identify the people arrested.

Agents made 646 arrests as part of the weeklong operation, officials said.

Officials allege those arrested included 140 people charged with or convicted of homicide, aggravated assault or domestic violence; 34 charged or convicted of a sex offense; 38 convicted of illegal firearms offenses; 52 charged or convicted of narcotics offenses; 51 charged with or convicted of property crimes; and 93 charged with or convicted of driving while intoxicated.

The arrests came as part of a targeted operation between Feb. 23 and March 2 meant to help public safety and national and border security, according to a spokesperson for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The dates coincide with a that began with an by Texas Gov. Greg Abbott. "These collective efforts have made our local communities significantly safer and strengthened our national security and border security," said Chad Plantz , special agent in charge for Homeland Security Investigations in Houston, in a prepared statement. Federal officials have been mostly mum about the specifics of their actions across the Houston region in recent weeks. In Monday's announcement, they said federal investigators had executed 71 warrants and arrested more than 543 people accused of crimes and seven gang members as part of the operation. They did not identify the people arrested. Agents made 646 arrests as part of the weeklong operation, officials said. Officials allege those arrested included 140 people charged with or convicted of homicide, aggravated assault or domestic violence; 34 charged or convicted of a sex offense; 38 convicted of illegal firearms offenses; 52 charged or convicted of narcotics offenses; 51 charged with or convicted of property crimes; and 93 charged with or convicted of driving while intoxicated. Monday's announcement did not explain how investigators know the seven arrested were gang members. The number of arrests includes almost 100 that weren't in the list of those charged with crimes. | | Dear Friend,

Learning about how early Christians worshipped and prayed, faced persecution and hardship, and settled theological disputes enriches our understanding of the faith. These lessons are especially important today, as Christians face increasing opposition from the culture.

But, beyond reading the New Testament and some of the stories of early Christian martyrs, it can be daunting to figure out how to proceed. The complicated history of imperial Rome, along with the foreign names and locations featured in early Christian history, can make understanding the most important historical points difficult.

To uncover this fascinating history, we've produced our online course, "[Ancient Christianity](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z2o55n38bm25l3i0a7cc4qka4nhtbuvdo5104dt0_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cdge1p34c3h2bs)," now available on DVD.

In this course, Professor Kenneth Calvert is your guide through the first four centuries of Christianity as he explains the remarkable ways the new faith transformed the Roman world.

Would you help support this course so we can make it available to millions of Americans for free? As a token of our appreciation for your support, we'll send you a copy of our beautiful DVD Box Set for any donations of $100 or more.

| | Dear Friend,

Learning about how early Christians worshipped and prayed, faced persecution and hardship, and settled theological disputes enriches our understanding of the faith. These lessons are especially important today, as Christians face increasing opposition from the culture.

But, beyond reading the New Testament and some of the stories of early Christian martyrs, it can be daunting to figure out how to proceed. The complicated history of imperial Rome, along with the foreign names and locations featured in early Christian history, can make understanding the most important historical points difficult.

To uncover this fascinating history, we've produced our online course, "[Ancient Christianity](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zaajhjqg5magh14p0ocad932ofjerpccin825q7o_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cdie0o74cdh2bs)," now available on DVD.

In this course, Professor Kenneth Calvert is your guide through the first four centuries of Christianity as he explains the remarkable ways the new faith transformed the Roman world.

Would you help support this course so we can make it available to millions of Americans for free? As a token of our appreciation for your support, we'll send you a copy of our beautiful DVD Box Set for any donations of $100 or more.

| | Dear Friend,

Learning about how early Christians worshipped and prayed, faced persecution and hardship, and settled theological disputes enriches our understanding of the faith. These lessons are especially important today, as Christians face increasing opposition from the culture.

But, beyond reading the New Testament and some of the stories of early Christian martyrs, it can be daunting to figure out how to proceed. The complicated history of imperial Rome, along with the foreign names and locations featured in early Christian history, can make understanding the most important historical points difficult.

To uncover this fascinating history, we've produced our online course, "[Ancient Christianity](https://links.conservativelibertywire.com/s/c/9P7LeMk2VGrwk1j93PVn7Eo6wMLRZ4gXeaKoU54knFfrbxTnNxNFu7x65HC5BOlOCa1Z0Mhbdij1SkTK2QMHNeAV6kwrwXIObq-DVksMAcg-6-WV7psg1t0nh4FgslNHSxrXkEZ2GtCs-8AwkInOB1nc_7ECEQiattYu2m52aydA-FIxAGMZRmZrVf1xFP5L2dBfKKl0zRkhUl0X1jSJUqb9CpwSdLQD3axKzG4kXdpayirs1uiUOeFKMtWCH1F82GSAmpaspWWX_lNeYRMcBo60n76_eVOf4yRYFuT0TYWVvvyhfMlCINsY-0zgOKteDwpndaNAIMfXOwILGjCjpuoCwg6rSPBhGGLV_xr6WWTk-ANITMwlyAD6vz_PhksjBU-HN7p6xA9YRQBa6JPEsEzsIVV9wvxJJQrwjTijBFYgY6s6tTz9CzPCXlRr4042nmK2cnBrsgkZrxGcA-4APpX4Zf-LGnjslCV035Pqv1KbhWqTuUmtdOj8IQ/U-4IYAFruZlJXhCzpKD8JwqUj7QnVjJL/6)," now available on DVD.

In this course, Professor Kenneth Calvert is your guide through the first four centuries of Christianity as he explains the remarkable ways the new faith transformed the Roman world.

This sponsored message from Conservative Liberty Wire is on behalf of Hillsdale College | | | | | Dear Friend, Learning about how early Christians worshipped and prayed, faced persecution and hardship, and settled theological disputes enriches our understanding of the faith. These lessons are especially important today, as Christians face increasing opposition from the culture. But, beyond reading the New Testament and some of the stories of early Christian martyrs, it can be daunting to figure out how to proceed. The complicated history of imperial Rome, along with the foreign names and locations featured in early Christian history, can make understanding the most important historical points difficult. To uncover this fascinating history, we've produced our online course, "," now available on DVD. In this course, Professor Kenneth Calvert is your guide through the first four centuries of Christianity as he explains the remarkable ways the new faith transformed the Roman world. Would you help support this course so we can make it available to millions of Americans for free? # Tuesday, March 11, 2025
---|---
**Good Morning!** On this day 136 years ago, the [Great Blizzard of 1888](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx00LFuwyAUheGnwRsWXGODB4Yu3tK1owXmEt-KhAhQLOfpq1RdO3_SOdL_dVkvjhLdr5_uhrbFvIKAkYuBS7kGR-lcVRdsRAQcOrRSKzkZI2Dudjuh8nHY1Ky910qNXqFXGnSQRk-ziB3Z95oYpJRCGBh7JXDUANEYLeLsN6YEBmq59N-Z7m3HmM78xNJv-dYlu7f2qGz4YLAwWI7j6HeqLZfz7QyWtlPlwZ2c7vxPGCzXgq5xn-j1ciXwHLkxfKdWObra-JZdbV2x4XFQSlQnzZS43hyl39f2X4WnhZ8AAAD__86OX6E), one of the worst blizzards in American history, struck the Northeast, killing over 400 people and dumping up to 55 inches of snow in certain areas. Today, the nation honors the itinerant American wanderer John Chapman on [Johnny Appleseed Day.](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0z7GOhCAQxvGngc7NMIpgQXGN3V57pUEZ1tkgGCV78e0ve9U113758kv-X_fp7jlxfnz6jVyNZUJA3UDbKDUFz-maOhlcJEJqJTllOtVbCzjI1WlSy9wboqhmM2gT7dx6bQaCgBotSnZvDVqlFIBFfeuAtEGM1hqIw7yIDihwLcftWTjXlWK6youO21I2mdxa636K9kPgKHDMvnLJPtUS_PV-_NmaZ1lzvhq_74lOotAEfwkc5eHC_s0p8dkb0cFj85x-9fpf7cvhTwAAAP__RahXWA) Chapman introduced apple trees across the frontier, though mainly as a source of apple cider for pioneers who often lacked access to clean drinking water. Today we're sponsored by our friends at [LMNT](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0j7Fu7CAQRb8GurWGMRgoKF7jbl-b0sIwrCfBZuWgjfbvo43Spr73HOm8XZdr5MrH7X_cKfTSFgQ0FxgvSi05cn0uWuZQiJBGSUFZrSbnAL3cwppdSj5F8Gv2aoxgbKRp9VMyQDkmyeFlg1EpBeDQDBrIWMTinIXi1yQ0UObezuG98dE3KvXZHnQOqe2yhq33uxj_CZwFzvnk46PuR3-NAuffqzxDvn9xrfw5WaHhtkeuP3z_q-cR8DsAAP__071NIg), who offer the best way to stay hydrated this spring.
|

## X Platform Hit by Major Hack Attacks
Elon Musk's [X was hit by a large-scale cyberattack](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kL1uwzAMBp9G3mRQ9J8yaOjiLV07GopFxywUK5DYqHn7Itk7fx_ugPs6L2fPkY_rp7-Rky0tCDho6LQxS_Acn0vfBLcRIXUNOTP1ZrQW8NTsjtBOUxj9OAJ224rUX4jwggMB2EBrw-5Fg84YA2BxaHugYULcrJ1gO11W1QMFlpTb78SH7LTFZ3pQbtd0a6LbRe5FdR8KZ4VzrbUVWvfsg38_FM4H1aJwjvwghfOv5qJDqoeOXqiIfs06HVoqi1AuWnbOQacf8Vdqsgv3yjFyGSfVw_XmOb7N8l-Jh8O_AAAA__-4sGHV) on Monday, triggering multiple separate outages that left tens of thousands of users unable to access the social media platform. The pro-Palestinian hacker group Dark Storm Team claimed [responsibility](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0j7FuwyAQQL_GbFjHgW08MHTJlq4dLRKOhAaHCF9M8_dVund_ek_v67gcfcrpfvn0KzmOZUHAQYKWSi3Bp_xajAguEiFpQU5NRo3WAs7i6uw8DBRQj0jBajiNOFKc5hB8PNlotEjubQOtlAKwOPQGaJgQo7UTxPl07gxQSFxq_13Sna8U86vsVPtzWUV2V-bH1umPDg8dHlpr_Z3a1ohub6DDw4_klpipyvJkfyEZfL3JjUtdZU47yecjeKZNIhjUWovqwqOlnNM2Tp2By-pT_ovxf_O7w98AAAD__6TkXDo), and Musk suggested a foreign country may also be involved. [Tech site Downdetector](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0z7FuwyAQgOGngS3RcYDBA0MXb-na0cJwjqmwiexrrLx9le7df33S_3Ubb7HUst0_40qB5zYioL2Avig15ljqazQyh5kISUsKyhnVeQ_YyyX0KWfwnY8YrU_a6klFa0Bp69PkXJQlvDXQSikAj_ZqgKxDnL13MPdTEgYoF2779buVjRea66s9ab-mtsoaFubHIfSHwEHgkNu5ZWJK7z61VeBwcOSfQ-DAZ2GmXeAg95AfZ6m1HJ0TBu5rLPXP4__-ngF_AwAA__8oxVGd) reported more than 40,000 outage complaints, with the heaviest disruptions along the U.S. coasts.
## Ships Collide, Explode, Spill Jet Fuel
Officials confirmed that [a U.S. tanker carrying jet fuel](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0j7FuxCAQRL8Gd1iwYOMrKNK4u7QpLWyW8yYcWIDOur-PnD7dSKOZp_d1X-6OIqXHp3uibSEvIGDgQnEpF-8ovhfdeRsQAVWHVhotx2kScOt2O-h1lDJ4p1dl1CpW49TohxCCN4OcXEf2ehNKSinEBEOvBQ4GIEyTEeG2bkwL9NRy6b8zpbZjiO_8wtJv-dlFu7d2VKY-GMwM5vM8-22tCc969QzmKzKYtxwjVcqJZ4q8ufSDhW-uPDKvOx085dJ2XtExmLti_XHSNRgN0-LxdBT_cO0__ZeF3wAAAP__gKZdcA) was struck by a container ship in the North Sea off England’s coast on Monday, causing multiple explosions, fires on both vessels, and a fuel spill. The [Portugal-registered Solong](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx00DFvwyAUBOBfgzesx7ON8cDQxVu6drQwPGJaAhGgWPn3lbt3O-mT7qT7um03E2JI90_zIN183hBw4jBwITZnQnxvY-e0J0IaOtJiHoVUCnDpDu1JTs7vYlgc7Ep67wygclbaeZfDYrqgrzYYhBAACqd-BJpmRK_UDH7ZLRuBXGi59N85pHaQj-_8otLb_OiiPlp7VjZ8MFwZrud59mm3ic56OcP1ihfkEh3DNYfIm0k_VLg15Z75i2qlyG2OMTjiKZd28EqGF5uMWCYJoivaPc8QY6hyZiPcHybEv_n23x0vjb8BAAD__-cZYvc) container ship collided with the anchored MV Stena Immaculate, an American-registered ship, rupturing a tank of Jet A-1 fuel intended for U.S. Navy ships. Lifeboats and aircraft were dispatched to the scene, and all 36 mariners across both crews were rescued, with one person taken to the hospital. [See rescue footage here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0z7GOhCAQxvGngW7NMKJgQXGN3V57pUEd1rmgGCWSffuL12_3JV_yS_4_z-HpOfL2-vYruRzSgIDNA-qHUsPsOb4HLWcXiJBqSU4ZrVprATu5uBa64DUZDEQWvTeqC8GP3QheE4CW7G4NaqUUgMWm0kCNQQzWGgjdOAkNNHNOR_WbeMsLhfhOFx3VlFYZ3ZLzfor6S2AvsC-lVOM43Z_AfqNyCuwvnindYzKNUbu-9qtJ8nDzXjhGPlsjNLxWz_HfzJ8aL4d_AQAA__-fulJy). The cause of the [crash remains undetermined](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kL9uszAUxZ_GbEbXFwNm8PANn6UOyZJKGZFrX8CVwQicoLx9RdS149GRfufP_dJfbIhhGa92Jp2H1CNgzaHiQvTehvjqZeH1QIRUFaRFK0WjFGBXTFpKdLa14DxQpUhSQyCpqTunROMbKoI-aVAJIQAU1qUEqlvEQakWhu7LMQnkQ05b-Z3Ckica4is9aStdmouop5zXnVX_GBqG5jiO8rGG02NoPtPaX-nYGZp72qLnv-JMZGigYmgEMDT_lzHaxfN9CuvO3Wb3id8yLZZ_zLN1j2gz8VuKaRkZmrZr3htFW9Unoti0X48QY9iblkkYZxviu17-666nxp8AAAD__5ZLaKo), though heavy fog was reported at the time of the incident.
## Biden Officials Lose Security Clearance

# **Free Speech Is Under Attack—We Won’t Stay Silent**
---
|
---
| | | | Hello friend, The attack on free speech should send shivers down everyone's spine—it certainly does mine. If Trump and the Anti-Defamation League, now a white supremacist group, don’t like what green card holder and graduate student Mahmoud Khalil had to say, they sure as hell won’t like what we have to say. The suffocating control that the Israeli lobby has over our government—Democrats and Republicans alike—has been exposed to the American people, and we will not be silenced any longer. That is why, for the first time, No Dem Left Behind will be active in Democratic primaries, targeting members who have shown they can no longer be trusted. What we are seeing on social media is that even the far right has joined in on the call to force AIPAC and other powerful “Israel first, America second” groups to register as foreign agents. The endless cycle of bowing to war criminal Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right genocidal government will no longer be tolerated by the American people. Regardless of political affiliation, Americans value our freedom of speech above all else—and we will not stay silent while a white supremacist, Nazi-loving administration attempts to take it away. This is just the beginning. As the markets continue to freefall, Trump and his enablers will become even more vocal, actively arresting and attempting to deport students whose political views they don’t like. They will try to dominate the news cycle with these arrests, distracting from the collapsing market and historic cost increases affecting everyday Americans. But we can chew gum and walk at the same time. We can—and must—focus on both issues. Canada has already implemented part of its retaliatory tariffs, and now people in Minnesota, Michigan, and the Dakotas are facing energy bills that are about $100 higher per month. That’s just one example of how Trump is making American lives more difficult and expensive to feed his own delusions. When asked about a possible recession, he simply shrugged. Excuse me? A recession—caused by his enablers and worshippers—less than a full quarter into his miserable presidency? And then there’s the other Nazi—the one the white supremacist ADL defended after he literally hailed Hitler. We aren’t allowed to say this on social media because we’ll be censored for "hate speech," but that’s exactly what he did when he performed a Nazi salute. Who among us has ever “accidentally” done that—especially after a speech? Yet the ADL insists, "Don’t believe your eyes—that’s not what Elon Musk was doing." Just like they tell us, "Don’t believe your eyes—Israel isn’t committing genocide." Meanwhile, Musk is openly admitting his next target: cutting entitlements. In a Fox Business interview, he stated that Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid are the hardest things to cut—meaning he wants to gut them. Republicans in poorer states rely on these programs to survive. Democrats believe people should not only survive, but thrive. In these past two months, we've raised over $8.3 million (what most representatives raise in a two year cycle), have recruited tens of thousands of volunteers in district and from all fifty states, have hired a team of over a hundred paid staff the majority being canvassers who are knocking over 10,000 doors a day. Even if they were right that a literal miracle would be required to win, I believe we are on the cusp of one. Miracles are happening every day here. Just last week, we were more than $53k off from our vital end of month target, donations were rapidly slowing down, and less than three hours remained on the clock. | | | | | == | | | | Screenshot of where we stood on Actblue last Friday night after my desperate call for support. I sent out an emergency request for aid, and our supporters delivered a small miracle (see above). But faith alone and our past achievements will not yield the miracle we need here. Will is what brings miracles to life. Collectively hundreds of thousands of your peers from every corner of this nation are making it happen. You are flying in to knock doors, phone banking, sending postcards, donating, and more. That work is what will materialize the miracle in Florida's 6th Congressional District. == | | | | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process immediately. | | | | | == | | == | | | | | == | | == | | | | | == | | == | | | | | == | | | | == | | | | As a supporter you have brought a literal miracle to within arms reach. ## Implementing Drones for School Security
An Austin-based company called Campus Guardian Angel [demonstrated](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00DGTgyAUBOBfgx0OD4lIQXGNXa690nnhoTKDkBESzb-_Sa6-fne_mf25TlcMMaTlGzdv6znnSQp54aLjABNhiK9JNWRvggw03oJW0BsxdLJZLVEPgwahySjjALubG1A6NQ9kkPTQBPseEx0AiIvu-laRgV54kv3FGDUjU8JTqHlv6-qrP7HM8ZWffm9d3ppo11rvhXVfTI5MjsdxtHM-NT5KDekdYXJM_ihMjrTn5At3uN0fhS8P3Clg4pgWH_lfgX8AXtyac-RlzbmGtJRmt3Q_Qoyh9JopsWwY4sev_x7ytPI3AAD__xlbZZ8) its innovative drones in a former elementary school building on Sunday. The drones can quickly respond to active shooter situations. Small enough to navigate indoor environments, the drones are equipped to [deploy flash bangs](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0z7FugzAQxvGnsbegO9uYMHhoVaVDlE6VOqIDH8GVKREYHN6-onvX75N-0v_r1twoxPBz_6CRXXr2U6NAlSfQJ8TGU4h7Y6R3LfgaJTusDNoazlrJwXnolK6qkjpou94iIQCX4D1ZVkhWBndgoBERykrbwvgaLbBXtqxr05MwwD6kaS7SwImftPRxnzaei24aZXRDSo9F6BehLkJdcs7FPq1pbfn4j4VSNwh92YR-u36-vsP3NdN6lrPzjxxiDIuthIH7SCH-kenfxs2p3wAAAP__zVtS1A) and discharge pepper balls. Co-founders Justin Marston and Bill King, a 32-year veteran of the Navy SEALs, said they were inspired by military drone usage in the Russia-Ukraine war. "_Our goal is to respond in five seconds, to be on the shooter in 15 seconds, and to degrade or incapacitate in 60 seconds_ ," said Marston. In May of 2022, it took law enforcement [more than 70 minutes](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00L-O8yAQBPCnsTsiFjCYguJr0uVrr7T2YIlXIiYyXP68_cnprxyN9NNovi7LBbnwdv2PNwr9leuipJqE1AJgScjlvZgxhW-ZPIwUwBmwXs5ajWsgSpTAYM4Zvc0uqzg5lGhjzGQnOXI4MKkBQE5O25NJHqykpOzkvck4GEmJe91PfaVOL2y5vOuD9lOst7GEtfd7G_S_QZ0Hdcb7Rs92VEfYO8dCgzq3tdbO27WJjyAo_UTsXDfx4FpoiyRaXGstQgMi6Mm6Oc8AMyVv0-w1oXMxz4TjHtL9yaVws24w8npDLp8p_c9vHkH9BgAA___PnGdW) to engage the shooter at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde. Boerne ISD has already agreed to participate in the program. State Rep. Ryan Guillen (R-Rio Grande City) has filed legislation that would increase funding for school security, including the hiring of more security officers and the [implementation of a drone response program](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00LHO4yAQBOCnwR0WrAGbguIad7n2SmtjlhgdDhZwcfz2p6T_6xl9Gs2f23LDmOLz8Rt3cu0d8gICNBcDl3LxGNO1qM67u_BWduTkqKSxYhqg2xyaYTCk9Kq8URMKi0YQTBCm8a5Byy66DyYGKaXQ42B65a00gjwYba0KyJQgH1sufduo0RtrSFd-UenXvHfJba0dlQ2_GMwM5vM8-7-vf_QJGcxYWlwTMZifdFYGc8orJgbzF_oWdvLcl_ykyuu65Zx4xUDt4g0rlcoPOg4qvB4FLwYzGMvXQGFFAk5mClyRJY5Imk_3UQVrLaCmrjh_nDGlWM3IlHjsGNN3cvvxw5eD_wEAAP__Eu5yww).
## Residents Oppose Burnet Quarry
A coalition of Burnet residents, including the local state representative, is [trying to stop the development](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLuOqzAUAL_GdEZ-gwsXt6HLbbdExj6EozU2Mk5I_n6V7bcfjUbzdZtvHhPm-3-_g2uvtcyCCU2ZpJzP0WN6z6qLbmHR8g4cHxQ3lo1SdJuLOnhtdRjXBSCsUq0L1wAhasmNjUOH7iNjknPO9CBNr6LlhkEURlurVk8Ug4it1L5t0ODlzzW9yxNqH8reJbe1dpxE_iNiImK6rqvf36fPPreSsXwgIqYM10nElErwiYjJ14YhARHT8qgZGq0lfNNQH-eG-U6P5HOjDXdImIEKxkclzNgf29FVF48LU8LTDESx--4x_Za0P9c8nfgJAAD__2rgZ98) of a proposed rock crushing plant over concerns about potential air, water, and noise pollution. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) [approved an air quality permit](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kDFvgzAQRn-N2Yzswzhh8NCFLV07ogs-4BSDqe1C8u-rdO_86Xt6el-34YYceJs_cSVXnlMcQEErVSO1HjxyeA2m8u6ufKcrcvpitO3UtYFqcXY07b0jaJvWaAsEHd79pIyCKyplx4rdG6YarbVqL42tje-0VeTBtl1nJhRGkecSU10WKvTEPIVXPCjVY1yr4JZS9iyaDwG9gP48z_rxxO09Cuh5OygXnrFw3LKAfoxbSe93ZgwyxfEhx_STF0pyjQdlOcV0YvJyiiHEk7dZlpG-5U5p5SJx31M8MAjoq-T8fnIInO1FGDWvyOHPqfwb6XDwGwAA__8wT2zW) for Asphalt Inc. last month, stating in a 31-page response to opponents’ concerns that “all applicable statutes, rules, and regulations would be met.” The Lower Colorado River Authority (LCRA) is currently reviewing how the proposed site would affect water quality at nearby Lake Buchanan. Staffers at Camp Longhorn on Inks Lake, which is downstream from Lake Buchanan, have said they are [“deeply concerned” about the impact](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kL2O6yAQRp8Gd1iA8V9BcRt3ue2WFoaJjYI9aMBx8varpN_6-3R0dH5u882GGI71v93BlNcdZyVUy0XDpZy9DfE968qbRfhRVmBkr2U3iqFR1WYWKQdtnW-XphtFa4dhbEWvPSwSrHBLFcwHJhoppWj7pqu1H2UnwKuuHUd9t0wL8KEg1WWDAi-b7_GNT6Da4V5Fs5WSMmv-MTUxNV3XVT9e9viMTE3heEIuYbUl4JGZmiIe64Z0cLKH24C4s3viPhC4gsQvJArgeSJMmMFzQvfgjs78_eIZPU8Y41mAX7YA8XymFN9MTRUZn64QY8hdz7RYdxvi17H8Ge1p1G8AAAD__-0xc24) the project could have on the organization’s 7,000 annual campers. State Rep. Ellen Troxclair (R-Lakeway) has filed legislation that would prohibit such projects within two miles of a youth camp and require environmental impact studies to be conducted before quarries can be developed in sensitive areas. "_I remain cautiously optimistic that our advocacy will eventually help the company to realize that this is not a place where they should be_ ," said Troxclair.
## Experience the Titanic in Dallas
_Titanic: The Exhibition_ has [returned to Dallas after 25 years](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00DGvozAQBOBfYzojezFwFC446ehy5V2JFrwOlgyO7E1I_v0Tr3_tjPRpNP9v8w1DDMf9L-5k-e3TDApaqRqp9ewwxM9sKmcX5QZdkdW90d2gfjVQbRbWdfCeVLcoRWBWjc1A_QqA3UKmhSrYC1ON1lq1fdPVxg26U-Sga4fBeBRGkQuccs0bMb2x-PhJL8r1mvYq2o35UUQzCpgETOd51ns5rk7ARId8FgETZ3xRFDAl3ihfQWA8wirpvYUlcEiHzMTPfBTJSTqMEYtEz5TlmXJ0Z3AkHylzkcnLFeOFYZbjqMfff_6VKlv3OEOMoXS9MOq-Y4jfA_nHx14WvgIAAP__pq1vxg), transforming a former retail space into an immersive experience with artifacts, recreated rooms, props from the blockbuster movie, and personal stories. The 25,000-square-foot exhibit was designed by [creative producer Mark Lach](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00L2O5CAQBOCnwRkjGmN8DggucTaXXmi1TXvcEoYR9M3P259mN968vlKp_l6XK3LifPuDJwV57WWxxg7a9BpgicjpvbguhtXECToKMDrwk_nV2-4IayQH27qDWz3E1XtjB7f5kdD66AfoOHzKTA8AZhh7f3FxAm8oWj9Mk9tROUORpdSLHCT0wrand3lQvWzl7FI4RO5N9b-VnZWdI6aEjXMuDxRqn4yys7Bg5k3T6-CVhUvWleRfzU1L0d9GP1kOjVV4x02abgffdSW9VcKPaBpz1GeppOzc1RDvT06Jmx-VM7cTOX0Nkh8fegT7PwAA__9oEmvQ) and Imagine Exhibitions CEO Tom Zaller, whose company currently operates 45 different exhibitions in nearly a dozen countries. They aim to sell 100,000 tickets before closing on May 11. The exhibit includes more than 350 artifacts from RMS Olympic, Titanic’s identical twin, and a virtual reality experience that helps visitors get a feel for what it’s like to explore the ship’s wreckage. Every guest [receives a “boarding pass”](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLuOszAQRp8GOiPfcOzCxd_Q5W-3RAMewkgOjuxRSN5-tZd26-_T0dH5uM5XoEzH7T_cMfJrK7OWehTSCKXmBJTfs-1TXGQKqseoLla5IL3R_R69CatDNaKCTXpj_bJ5XLzHZFZ0wfUUv2DSKKXkeDFusCkoJzFpN4ZgN-isxERc6sA7Mr6gbfldnliHtdz7HHfmR-vMv05PnZ7O8xwS5AytLA3r763TE1RunZ5-NsHEcNAqeEeBr50WYiqHoCbgEHQwVliZnih2alzqW2RsrRxCK6ODUWNfY3qclDM1d-msvN2B8rcQ_1noGfVnAAAA__8IHmqa) with biographical information collected from a real passenger or crew member prior to the ship’s April 1912 voyage. [Tickets to the exhibit](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0z7FugzAQgOGnsbegu7MxePDQhS1dOyLDmXCSgQislLx9Rffsvz7p_7n39yhZ1sd3XFIo57T1BFTfwNwQe46S373VHAZgjzoFbCw6D60hPQfrE7RjOzEzDuSIaawNR2dhQnDtqCVcGBhEhLoxrrLs0UFicrX3dorKQmIp216VOZV0xmPK7-2V9mrcFp3DXMrzUOZLUaeouxopcZUxnbMMUmRbr1BRxzHneCjq9B74-Ss5y-EaZeGxRMn_Wvm49wr0FwAA__93Q1I2) start at $25. body:
The 1860s brought war to the doorsteps of many Americans, but none as literally as Wilmer McLean, who witnessed the beginning and end of the Civil War from his own home.

# [The Civil War started and ended on the same person’s property.](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssyhk7&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
### [U.S. History](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssyhk7&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
[](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssyhk7&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
| T he 1860s brought war to the doorsteps of many Americans, but none as literally as Wilmer McLean, [who witnessed](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssyhk7&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) the beginning and end of the Civil War from his own home. McLean and his wife, Virginia Mason, moved to Manassas, Virginia, in 1853, shortly after their wedding. A few years later, the couple was surprised when Confederate General P.G.T. Beauregard commandeered their property to serve as his headquarters ahead of the first major land battle of the Civil War, the First Battle of Bull Run (although several smaller skirmishes had been fought during the months prior). The home was so close to the action that a cannonball soared through the kitchen and landed in the fireplace. The battle ended on July 21, 1861, in a Confederate victory, and as the fighting continued, the McLeans decided to head south.
---
As fate would have it, by 1863, the McLeans were reestablished in a small village called Appomattox Court House in southern Virginia. On April 9, 1865, the couple received a knock on their door. It was Charles Marshall, the aide to Confederate General Robert E. Lee, asking for a secure meeting location for the general. McLean showed Marshall surrounding properties, but none was as suitable as his own home, which he eventually volunteered. Later that day, Lee arrived at the McLean house, followed by Union General Ulysses S. Grant. It was at this meeting in the parlor that Lee formally surrendered to Grant, signaling the end of the American Civil War.

## The “S” in Ulysses S. Grant’s name has no meaning.
Ulysses S. Grant was born Hiram Ulysses Grant on April 27, 1822, though as a child he often went by his middle name, Ulysses. In 1839, he applied to the United States Military Academy at West Point, and the benefactor who oversaw the application, Ohio Congressman Thomas Hamer, mistakenly wrote “Ulysses S. Grant” on the document, apparently taking the initial from Grant’s mother’s maiden name, Simpson, though Simpson was never Grant’s middle name. In fact, the erroneous “S” in Grant’s name doesn’t stand for anything, and Hiram, his real first name, was completely dropped — yet the name stuck. Grant’s attempts to correct the error were curbed by delays and more paperwork, so he eventually accepted his new moniker. In an 1844 letter to his future wife, Julia Dent, [Grant quipped](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssyhk7&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com), “Find some name beginning with ‘S’ for me.”

Grant’s name has no meaning. Ulysses S. Grant was born Hiram Ulysses Grant on April 27, 1822, though as a child he often went by his middle name, Ulysses. In 1839, he applied to the United States Military Academy at West Point, and the benefactor who oversaw the application, Ohio Congressman Thomas Hamer, mistakenly wrote “Ulysses S. Grant” on the document, apparently taking the initial from Grant’s mother’s maiden name, Simpson, though Simpson was never Grant’s middle name. In fact, the erroneous “S” in Grant’s name doesn’t stand for anything, and Hiram, his real first name, was completely dropped — yet the name stuck. Grant’s attempts to correct the error were curbed by delays and more paperwork, so he eventually accepted his new moniker. **This is an incredibly important read for anyone interested in or engaging in conversations about egg prices.** Monopolist egg producers are robbing us blind, the talking heads are parroting egg industry talking points because that's who is feeding them info, and the days of cheap protein seem gone forever.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/831a4296-e0f0-4072-bed9-4c0a33b01ab9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
1976, when normal guys could still afford eggs (Rocky)
Fortunately, former Missouri Lt. Gov. ([and Lucas Kunce for US Senate endorser](https://substack.com/redirect/680b0c64-a662-4294-8bcd-808d28ad51e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) Joe Maxwell's pro-family-farm organization, Farm Action, teamed up with antitrust expert [Basel Musharbash](https://substack.com/@baselmusharbash) to fight back for all of us. '
My former coworker, Matt Stoller, brings us the details below through his Substack, [BIG](https://substack.com/redirect/51bda3ae-5cd0-44e5-9dfd-e839d8b1dd57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which covers all things antitrust. This is the first installment of BIG's three part series on egg prices, so be sure to [subscribe to BIG to get the whole series](https://substack.com/redirect/51bda3ae-5cd0-44e5-9dfd-e839d8b1dd57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (just like mine, it's free, or you can become a paid supporter if you like).
Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9sdWNhc2t1bmNlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.nfJcjyH99ReWyfdOQRlh2A6j8MrR5-JYe4tyeWJoSjc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=158818145)
* * *
_This issue is part one of a three-part BIG series called Hatching a Conspiracy, on the egg industry. It is written by[antitrust lawyer Basel Musharbash](https://substack.com/redirect/4c7afdc5-ab3d-4bae-bb0d-0224775fb9f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), based in part on a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/c57e78f6-aee2-43f4-8b09-4c315a7018a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he researched for Farm Action._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ee162b94-a717-446f-af80-11064f83fb93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Over the past two months, egg prices have become a political football. Journalists are [reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/cdf148e5-26d6-4082-b19f-ea7ebb64511c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in depth on the industry, egg consolidation has come up in a Congressional antitrust [hearing](https://substack.com/redirect/655b4eb0-12cd-4b63-a1dd-e9b4846ef943?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and Donald Trump mentioned a plan to tackle egg prices in the State of the Union speech, putting his Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins on notice that she has to get the price down. Most notably, earlier this week, the Capitol Forum reported the Department of Justice Antitrust Division is now investigating egg markets.
The reason is simple. For most Americans, eggs have always been cheap, and thus a key food staple. And now eggs are expensive, and sometimes in shortage. Over the past year egg prices have increased by 53%-- [jumping](https://substack.com/redirect/604816c4-a8aa-4404-9278-e4dc9902aea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 15% in January alone. As of the beginning of February, egg producers were charging wholesale buyers an [average of $5.95 for a dozen eggs](https://substack.com/redirect/0ca1cb7f-4b87-4d48-9023-fb1e28262869?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and retailers were charging consumers anywhere [between](https://substack.com/redirect/61567369-5265-4c31-8b10-9034524e065d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [$4 and $9 a dozen](https://substack.com/redirect/e9312915-2e68-4437-9fe4-542570950b85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- and sometimes even more.
The high prices, and sometimes shortages, are a problem in and of themselves, but they also represent that the American system has gone askew. If we can't even get a cheap omelet or egg sandwich anymore, what can America do right?
The stated reason for the high price of eggs is something that happens periodically: an avian flu epidemic. Since 2022, outbreaks of bird flu on poultry farms have led to the culling of over [115 million egg-laying hens](https://substack.com/redirect/488f3a09-56e3-470d-bcfb-5353dcbe0a55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This epidemic, according to the prevailing narrative, has driven egg prices up to record highs all on its own. As one industry executive [put it](https://substack.com/redirect/c68d7d76-17ed-4573-b771-c2ae2c34e774?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it's all just "supply disruption, 'act of God' type stuff." The popular response to this story has been what you'd expect: Scientists are discussing flu vaccines for chickens, politicians are blaming each other about bird culls, and many are concerned about how the massive scale of today's egg farms enables--and exacerbates--avian flu epidemics. And none of that is necessarily wrong.
But something doesn't add up about this "avian flu is the sole and natural cause of high egg prices" story. Despite the "act of God" going on -- and the skyrocketing prices accompanying it -- egg production is actually . . . not down by all that much. 115 million hens is a lot of birds to cull, but it's important to put the loss of those hens in context: They weren't lost all at once. They were lost over three years. And there have always been around 300 million other hens alive and kicking to lay eggs for America--not to mention a continuous pipeline of 120-130 million female chicks (called "pullets") in the process of being raised into adult hens to replace the ones dying or aging out.
As a result of this pipeline, the effect of avian flu outbreaks on egg production, while not insignificant, has been relatively small. Monthly egg production during each of the last three years has averaged only 3-5% lower than it was in 2021, the year before the epidemic started. Meanwhile, demand for eggs has actually declined. According to private reports by the Egg Industry Center, Americans went from consuming around 206 shell eggs each in 2021 to consuming less than 190 shell eggs each in 2024 -- a ~7.5-percent nosedive. As many countries have closed their markets to American eggs since 2021 on account of the avian flu, egg exports have also fallen off a cliff -- going down by nearly half between 2021 and 2022 and staying there ever since. That dynamic, according to my analysis of USDA data, has shaved another ~2.5% off aggregate demand on U.S. egg production.
So, reports of an unprecedented egg "shortage" are exaggerated. Nonetheless, egg prices -- and egg company profits -- have gone through the roof. Cal-Maine Foods -- the largest egg producer and the only one that publishes its financial data as a publicly traded company -- has been making more money than ever. It's annual gross profits in the past three years have floated between _[](https://substack.com/redirect/11651f68-1dcf-4053-8693-c45115d4b737?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[3 and 6 times](https://substack.com/redirect/11651f68-1dcf-4053-8693-c45115d4b737?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) __ what it used to earn before the avian flu epidemic started -- [breaking $1 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/f3ae3451-5565-4229-a0d4-a2ab8e135068?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the first time in the company's history. All of this extra profit is coming from higher selling prices, which have been earning Cal-Maine [unprecedented 70-145 percent margins ](https://substack.com/redirect/11651f68-1dcf-4053-8693-c45115d4b737?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)over farm production costs per dozen. Taking Cal-Maine as the "[bellwether](https://substack.com/redirect/9686679e-be25-4eb0-8425-e41624786915?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" for the industry's largest firms -- as people in the egg business do -- we can be pretty confident that the other large egg producers are also raking in profits off the relatively small dip in egg production.
High persistent profits are an anomaly for the industry. Historically, egg producers have responded to avian flu epidemics--and the temporary rise in egg prices that often accompanies them--by quickly rebuilding and expanding their flocks of egg-laying hens. "[Fowl plagues](https://substack.com/redirect/1bfe528e-de0b-4730-8c9f-c5040a881d5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"--as these epidemics used to be called--have been with us since at least the 19th century. Most recently, large-scale avian flu epidemics hit egg farms in 2015 and 1983-1984. The egg industry responded to both of these destructive events by sprinting to rebuild and expand the egg-laying hen flock -- something which checked price increases and ultimately made sure prices went back to pre-epidemic levels within a reasonable time.
As Cal-Maine Foods explained in its [2007 Annual Report](https://substack.com/redirect/63c16319-6bf7-4958-8a95-a4957db414e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "In the past, during periods of high profitability, shell egg producers have tended to increase the number of layers in production with a resulting increase in the supply of shell eggs, which generally has caused a drop in shell egg prices until supply and demand return to balance."
For example, immediately after the height of the avian flu epidemic in May 2015, egg producers started adding millions more pullets to their operations each month--ultimately raising 15.3 million more pullets on their farms in 2015 than they did in 2014, and increasing that figure by another 8 million in 2016, according to my analysis of data from monthly USDA/NASS [Chicken and Eggs](https://substack.com/redirect/331d24db-2441-423c-bcd4-c018c7b24322?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reports. Altogether, producers added adult hens to their flocks at a prodigious rate of 4.15 million per month on average from August 2015 through February 2016, replacing nearly all of the hens lost to avian flu within 7 months.
As a result, the average wholesale price of eggs landed at $1.65 a dozen that year, only 40 percent higher than it did the year before. By the end of March 2016, monthly [egg production was higher](https://substack.com/redirect/4334aa1e-3181-40a5-9177-bcdfcd0f67bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than it was in March 2014 -- and egg prices had not only returned to pre-epidemic levels, but were [dropping even lower](https://substack.com/redirect/4334aa1e-3181-40a5-9177-bcdfcd0f67bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
This time around, however, that's not happening. Despite high profits, the egg industry has somehow maintained a stubborn deficit in egg production capacity. Hatcheries -- the firms that supply hens to egg producers -- have _throttled_ the pipeline of hens instead of expanding it. According to the Egg Industry Center, the size of the flock of "parent" hens -- the hens used by hatcheries to produce layer chicks for egg producers -- plummeted from 3.1 million hens in 2021, to 2.9 million in 2022, to 2.5 million hens in 2023 and 2024.
Meanwhile, hatcheries have been hatching significantly fewer parent chicks to replace aging ones -- nearly 380,000 (or 12 percent) fewer in 2022 compared to the year before, and even fewer parent chicks in 2023 and 2024 -- leaving the parent flock older and more likely to produce eggs that fail to hatch. That could explain why, although hatcheries reported producing 125-200 million more fertilized eggs to the USDA in each of the last three years compared to 2021, the number of eggs they've placed in incubators and the number of chicks they've hatched from those eggs has either declined or stayed basically steady with 2021 levels in every year since.

As for egg producers themselves, you may be surprised to learn that they have added between 5 and 20 million _fewer_ pullets to their farms in every one of the last three years than they did in 2021. As the USDA [observed](https://substack.com/redirect/4ccebef4-20a8-47db-a735-d8798a1eda4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with some astonishment at the end of 2022, "producers--despite the record-high wholesale price [of eggs]--are taking a cautious approach to expanding production[.]" The [following month](https://substack.com/redirect/19eb10cb-9504-4e3a-9708-9fbe23c01047?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it pared down its table-egg production forecast for the entirety of 2023 on account of "the industry's [persisting] cautious approach to expanding production."

In other words, the only thing that the egg industry seems to have expanded in response to the avian flu epidemic is windfall profits -- which have likely amounted to more than $15 billion since the epidemic began (judging by the increase in the value of annual egg production since 2022), and appear to have been spent primarily on stock buybacks, dividends, and acquisitions of rivals instead of rebuilding and expanding flocks. When an industry starts profiting more from *not* producing than from producing, it's a sign that something isn't right. It could be an innocent bottleneck. But when it lasts for three years on end with no relief in sight, it's usually a sign of something else that's pervasive in America -- monopolization.

As the coming installments in this series will detail, the fundamental problem in the egg supply chain today is the simple fact that every industry involved in turning an egg into a chicken and turning a chicken into an egg--from the breeders and hatcheries that create the hens to the producers who use the hens to make eggs--has been hijacked by one or two financier-backed corporations, with the incentives flipped from competing entities seeking to produce more eggs to an oligopoly trying to restrain the production of eggs.
On one end of the egg supply chain, you have two companies who control chicken genetics, the billionaire-owned [Erich Wesjohann Group](https://substack.com/redirect/be3f9e15-467f-4ccd-b01a-af4eccdc80e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the private-equity-backed [Hendrix Genetics](https://substack.com/redirect/a9c15587-943c-4cb5-a399-a812ed5ac2ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Headquartered a short car trip apart in Cuxhaven, Germany, and Boxmeer, Netherlands, these private firms have systematically gained control over the supply of egg-laying hens to American producers over the past two decades by buying out or suppressing rivals and challengers. Today, no egg producer in this country can expand the number of hens in its flock -- or even replace the hens it already has when they age out or die -- without the cooperation of this duopoly. And, since the value of hens rises with the price of the eggs, when the price of eggs is high these two barons have a clear interest in keeping the supply of pullets to producers on a tight leash -- so the high prices stick.
On the other end of the egg supply chain, you have the largest egg producer in the country and the world, Cal-Maine Foods.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/82295225-745b-42f3-9d08-dac261114fc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Cal-Maine isn't just the largest egg producer and distributor, but has a range of coercive tools at its disposal to discipline smaller rivals in the industry. Through what looks like [a special arrangement ](https://substack.com/redirect/e3a22faa-9fef-477b-8143-861ff0300e0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with the chicken-genetics barons, Cal-Maine can expand its output faster and cheaper than any other egg producer. If a producer gets out of line and responds to high prices with flock expansions or discounting practices that Cal-Maine doesn't approve of, Cal-Maine can flood the market with eggs--depressing prices for everyone while capturing market share for itself. As a publicly-traded company with a low cost of capital from Wall Street, Cal-Maine can live with low egg prices for a long time. Not so for most of the 60 or so family-owned producers who make up the rest of the egg industry; they're actual businesses that need to turn a profit.
The power wielded by these dominant firms -- EW Group, Hendrix, and Cal-Maine -- is not theoretical. Just last year, a federal jury found that, shortly after Cal-Maine rose to dominance in the late 1990s, its executives took over the leadership of a longstanding industry association called the United Egg Producers (UEP) and turned it into a cartel, the equivalent of what the presiding judge analogized to a "[mob boss](https://substack.com/redirect/2f8ac066-c23a-4ded-9eee-99127dc63e0d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" for the industry.
Shortly after, other major egg producers that had long resisted joining the UEP -- like Rose Acre Farms -- gave up their independence and entered the UEP's fold, until it finally represented producers accounting for more than 90% of the country's egg supply. Cal-Maine's executives then used the association as a "bullhorn" to "[bark out orders](https://substack.com/redirect/2f8ac066-c23a-4ded-9eee-99127dc63e0d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" at egg producers and "coordinate a conspiracy" to restrict the supply of eggs in the United States through a variety of strategies -- including throttling the replacement of hens lost to mortality and a fake "animal welfare" program designed to reduce overall flock numbers rather than improve hen's lives.
An economist who helped plan the UEP cartel [summed up](https://substack.com/redirect/ad5d6d81-92a3-41c4-8f22-dc6878942282?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the economic rationale behind it pretty simply: "More hens, less income!" And the conspiracy's results proved he was right. Wholesale egg prices reached unprecedented heights over the course of the 2000s and then never came back down -- settling around a new, higher focal point 50 to 100 percent higher than the pre-conspiracy level for the next decade. Something similar could be happening with the current avian flu epidemic. Indeed, the new focal point appears to be already here: There was an argument that wholesale egg prices "collapsed" in 2023. In reality, they were on average 75% higher than wholesale egg prices before the epidemic's onset in 2022.

One way to understand the problem of eggs is consistent with similar problems we're seeing in other parts of the economy. From [baby formula](https://substack.com/redirect/0d536183-ee86-4529-afe7-e2c471855ddf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [cancer drugs](https://substack.com/redirect/30213323-3368-4065-9664-fa38eeb8b06b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [beef](https://substack.com/redirect/ba12716e-03e8-4e27-9672-bdcceb522158?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), shortages and supply shocks in concentrated industries are now routine.
In other words, the current egg crisis is what the Sovietization of American business looks like. We don't have egg companies in the business of making eggs anymore. We have egg companies in the business of exploiting egg shortages, almost a private government of eggs. This dynamic is so extreme that the Agriculture Secretary had to go on something of a diplomatic mission to Cal-Maine [last month](https://substack.com/redirect/c94e051b-adb0-4ccb-bde4-b81f911cea6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to try to sweet-talk its executives into loosening their grip on the egg supply -- and walked out of her meeting saying the USDA is going _to pay egg producers_ to rebuild the country's hen flock __ at a time when rebuilding the hen flock is going to be more profitable for them than it has ever been.
So, that's the broad-brush picture. To understand how we got to this place where shortages are more profitable than production, we have to start with the origins of the American egg business. After all, there's a reason that a big cheap breakfast served in a diner on the roadside was such a big part of American culture, and why it's such a shock to see [Denny's levy an egg surcharge](https://substack.com/redirect/0f061504-fc66-4f84-856f-029f71274365?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). So let's start with how the big fluffy omelet became so Americana.
**America as a Land of Egg Plenty**
Producing an egg seems simple. An "old McDonald had a farm" kind of farmer breeds a lovely hen, grows it to adulthood, has it lay eggs, puts those eggs in a crate, and sends that crate to a grocery store in return for a negotiated price. And that's basically how the industry worked until the middle of the 20th century. The essentials of that story remained on point, but the components were split up among a series of specialized operations.
If you abstract out what the egg farmer used to do all by himself, you get all the layers of the modern egg supply chain. First, as discussed above, there are breeders, who manage chicken genetics and produce "parent stock," or the stock of birds that are mated to produce the fertilized eggs that become table-egg laying hens. Second, there are hatcheries, who buy parent stock from breeders, mate them to produce fertilized eggs, incubate their eggs to hatch table-egg laying chicks, and then grow the chicks into hens. Third, there are egg producers, who buy table-egg laying chicks or hens from the hatcheries and use them to produce eggs (some producers also buy fertilized eggs from hatcheries and incubate them in-house). Fourth, there are the various distributors and processors who buy eggs from producers. And finally, there are market reporters who survey buyers and sellers for information about egg prices and other market data points, and use that information to publish regular benchmarks for the market value of eggs.
So, to understand the story behind egg prices, we shouldn't think about "the egg industry" or the "egg market" but a series of linked industries and markets -- starting from the breeders and hatcheries, running through the egg producers and the egg buyers, all the way to the market reporters -- the end result of which is the carton of eggs on the shelf. To get there, we have to start eighty years ago, when egg production was revolutionized by new technologies and techniques, and the modern egg supply chain was born.
In 1942, New Deal-era Secretary of Agriculture, and then Vice President, Henry A. Wallace built a new model for producing eggs. It was based on creating better birds through the "hybridization" of chicken, which is the crossing of two or more pure breeds of chicken to create a "hybrid" chicken with specific qualities. The resulting hens laid more or better eggs, required less feed, and were more adapted to specific production systems. After Wallace developed them, cross-breeding methods were shared with small breeders around the country through United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) extension offices at land grant colleges, which conducted basic research into the field and made breeding know-how and pure-bred stocks available to the public. Within a few years, dozens of other "primary breeders" emerged, creating a dynamic chicken genetics industry with many local and regional players.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3821ac40-ed6e-4597-a87e-29d1d58a408e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

These primary breeders developed branded strains of layer chickens and marketed them to thousands of hatcheries nationwide. The hatcheries bought "parent stock" for branded strains of chicken from the primary breeders, mated them to produce fertilized eggs, incubated the eggs until they hatched, and then sold the resulting chicks and young hens (called "pullets") to farmers, which raised them into mature hens and then used them to produce eggs. As farmers got to know the different hybrid chicken brands, they selected among them for productivity and other characteristics that suited their production systems -- creating a virtuous feedback loop.
Soon, these developments led to a revolution in egg production both at home and around the world. The number of eggs laid per hen in the United States increased by almost [44% between 1940 and 1955](https://substack.com/redirect/6a36b667-9fe7-44f2-9e70-8e5c7f7b59e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- more, in relative terms, than it would increase over the next four decades combined. Hybrid hens originating from the United States were soon introduced around the world, leading to a rapid expansion in global egg production--not to mention the explosion in cheap American diners dotting the new highway systems being built.
In tandem with the mid-century revolution in chicken breeding, there was a revolution in egg production systems. Poultry science departments at land-grant colleges engaged in continual field testing and production research to develop new equipment and systems for egg farmers, ultimately developing critical technologies like large-scale incubators to hatch eggs on a schedule, fine-sand blowers to clean eggs without breaking shells, and caged-rearing systems to mechanize feeding, watering, and egg-collection in their hen houses.
Although these innovations gave rise to some efficiencies of scale at the farm level and enabled the rise of factory-style hatcheries and egg production facilities, the industry as a whole remained highly decentralized at every stage of production and distribution well into the late 1970s. As late as 1978, most producers were still small, and most egg production still took place on farms with [fewer than 50,000 hens](https://substack.com/redirect/b57c2796-4710-4084-8d5e-f049e065b5b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). There were just [34 "big" egg companies with 1 million or more egg-laying hens each](https://substack.com/redirect/861465ef-eabc-46bf-8e8c-633c9c6fdbf2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and they accounted for only 27% of annual egg production.
Undergirding this system was law: Antitrust enforcement prevented the largest breeders, hatcheries, and egg producers from growing by serial acquisitions or by handicapping their rivals' access to customers or suppliers. For similar reasons, the markets into which egg producers sold their eggs--packers, retailers, processors, wholesalers, and institutions--also remained open and competitive, offering a wide diversity of potential buyers to egg producers of various sizes in every region of the country.
Because of the openness of the egg industry and the abundance of small producers with excess capacity, there was almost always a significant surplus of eggs in the country. When that surplus narrowed (whether because of long-term population growth or a sudden crisis, like an avian flu epidemic), elevated egg prices invited rapid expansions in egg output from new and existing producers that quickly brought prices back down. For example, during the [avian flu epidemic of 1983-1984](https://substack.com/redirect/1dd2a361-f077-4dfc-95e3-0497b5a661ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), producers had to cull tens of millions of layer hens and other birds, including nearly every chicken in Pennsylvania. But retail egg prices rose by just 66 percent over a few months -- and promptly fell just as [sharply over the next few months](https://substack.com/redirect/1dd2a361-f077-4dfc-95e3-0497b5a661ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as producers quickly replaced the hens they'd lost.
"Eggs," [said](https://substack.com/redirect/c6f9ee04-c732-431f-848c-e301049e605b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a prominent agricultural economist in 1978, "will be processed and produced in this country if there is a fair return on investment. When the return [on eggs] becomes high," he continued, "there will be expansion of production that will reduce prices." And that was actually true: Higher prices routinely led farmers to get into the egg business to make money, and that in turn regularly reset the market with more supply. Price spikes were short-lived. Shortages were unheard of. America was a land of egg plenty.
Then, everything changed.

Gov. () Joe Maxwell's pro-family-farm organization, Farm Action, teamed up with antitrust expert to fight back for all of us. ' My former coworker, Matt Stoller, brings us the details below through his Substack, , which covers all things antitrust. This is the first installment of BIG's three part series on egg prices, so be sure to (just like mine, it's free, or you can become a paid supporter if you like).
